scope: Open review of benign lung tumors as a class, covering epithelial and mesenchymal lesions including papilloma and hamartoma.

keyRecommendations.text: Benign lung neoplasms are an uncommon group of epithelial and mesenchymal tumors, generally smaller than 3 cm.
Endobronchial lesions can cause cough, post-obstructive pneumonia, or hemoptysis; parenchymal lesions can be asymptomatic nodules.
Pulmonary hamartomas are benign mesenchymal neoplasms. Complete excision is recommended for papillomas because of recurrence and uncertain malignant potential.

clinicalBottomLine: Treat a benign lung tumor as a small epithelial or mesenchymal lesion whose symptoms depend on whether it is endobronchial or parenchymal. Hamartoma is a benign mesenchymal neoplasm, and papillomas are excised completely.
notableCaveats: The 2025 comprehensive review is not open. This 2008 class review was openly readable and covers more than a single hamartoma case.

source.title: Benign tumors and tumorlike conditions of the lung.
